inspected_facts: Actual get_terrain_3d_types_in_sector in terrdata.c:1747-1802 selects with get_terrain_3d_sector, clears all TERRAIN_TYPE_LAST scratch ints, flags the first unsigned-byte surface id, advances/flags each polygon surface_change and returns one plus transition count. The fixture does not substitute a distinct-type count or compute the expected surface answer.

Actual selected routine writes shared terrain_types_in_sector and sets rounding toward zero via sector selection; it does not mutate sector geometry, RNG, entities, campaign time or heap. The engine-entry numeric context and existing X1 conversion patch supply the current hosted truncating sector-selection behavior. This characterizes the unchanged helper on the present hosted baseline, not an unhooked whole original DLL.

Group10 is explicit-only and branches before the old witness dispatch; default/census/164-case tables are unchanged. The case plan has first/last/middle sectors, 48 sweep samples, finite neighboring-edge floats and sound clamp points. It retains raw IEEE input words and does not silently repair rejected coordinates.

Domain checks call the original selector and reject out-of-grid indices before grid indexing, missing surface table, missing polygon table when polygon count is positive, and surface ids beyond scratch bounds. surface_id is unsigned char, so a negative-id case is not omitted. Polygon/surface walking follows the original order. On valid loaded retail structures, generated finite coordinates stay in the relevant representable integer range.

Successful cases save scratch, fill two distinct sentinels for repeat/reset observations, conditionally interleave the reference sector, capture the resulting flags and restore saved bytes before output formatting. Output-capacity failure therefore occurs after restoration. Domain refusal precedes scratch filling, so it changes no scratch. Unavailable reference interleave is explicitly na/-1, not a fabricated success.

Lua writes raw original lines and complete flags, keeps returned/distinct/polygon counts separate, checks flags against derived count fields and requires restored=1. Repeat/reset/interleave differences are recorded as original anomalies rather than repaired. Checked write/flush/close failures and unavailable env_case cause witness failure; no frames are run by this driver.

Four Rust controls run the real Lua driver with scripted row/output collaborators, covering answered/rejected samples, return-versus-distinct separation, anomaly/restoration distinction, malformed rows/counts and output failures. They characterize driver bookkeeping only; they supply no physical terrain proof.

New wind34 receipts are a preservation checkpoint of the already reviewed actual wind evidence, with explicit mixed provenance and retained earlier failures. They were not used to infer sector results. No production provider, ABI, build flag, accepted driver, baseline or tolerance change is present.
